sections.sectionSummaryBrief: After stating "this day is the beginning of Your works," the verse adds "a remembrance of the first day," indicating that Rosh Hashanah as a remembrance of the first day is loftier than it being the beginning of Your works.

translations.translation: And after it says "this day is the beginning of Your works," it adds "a remembrance of the first day,"
for that Rosh Hashanah is a remembrance of the first day is loftier than that it is the beginning of Your works.
For "the beginning of Your works" is the perfection and renewal of creation that is brought about through the service of man
(as above),
for the drawing down from Above that comes through this is only from the level that arousal from below reaches there.
However, the matter of the first day is
(as the Tzemach Tzedek explains in the aforementioned discourse28)
that the drawing down then was from His own essence,
for there was not yet anyone to arouse, as it is written29
"and there was no man" etc.30
[That is,
not only was there no actual arousal from below, but it was not even possible for there to be arousal from below],
and the drawing down then was from His kindness,
for31
"He desires kindness."
That is,
in addition to the fact that the drawing down now
(through arousal from below)
is of the aspect of judgment and justice, while the drawing down then was from His kindness28,
"the world is built with kindness"32,
this kindness
(of the first day)
is above not only kindness as it is in the emotions, but also above its root as it is in the intellect, etc.,
for its essence is
(not kindness, but)
"desire for kindness,"
the matter of desire
(delight33),
except that the desire is that there be kindness,
and from this it is drawn that "the world is built with kindness,"
for from this desire the kindness is built, from which the world is built34.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The inner reason the first day of creation is called "first day" is that the revelation of the desire for kindness that shone on that day is the first light and revelation, the cause and root of the attribute of kindness from which all worlds came into being.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the inner reason why the first day of creation is called "first day" is,
that the revelation of the desire for kindness that shone on this day is a light and revelation
("day" is light and revelation)
that is first,
which is the cause and root for the drawing down of the attribute of kindness from which all worlds came into being.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: On Rosh Hashanah, by recalling the manner of creation on the first day when the revelation of the desire for kindness shone, this revelation is drawn down, making it loftier than the aspect of "beginning of Your works" which comes through arousal from below.

translations.translation: And this is "a remembrance of the first day,"
that on every Rosh Hashanah,
by recalling the manner of creation that was on the first day,
when the revelation of the desire for kindness shone,
through this they draw down35
this revelation.
And this is that the matter that Rosh Hashanah is a remembrance of the first day is loftier than that Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of Your works,
for "the beginning of Your works" is what is drawn down through arousal from below,
while the first day
(the revelation of the desire for kindness)
is the first light and revelation that is the root and cause of the entire order of Hishtalshelus
(above and below),
and it itself is above the category of above and below
(upper and lower).
